fields.reasoning: The change set's intent is that a bring-your-own workflow runs end to end under the daemon, and the owner's words (source byo-daemon-plan-research) ask that a BYO workflow run end to end. The leaf byo-workflow-daemon-e2e forbids changing docs/examples/byo/*.toml, which rules out (b), and the example is the documented level-3 team workflow, so making every team add a Rhiza review would contradict bring-your-own. (c) adds a new workflow field and file-format surface only to restate what the workflow already says by having no review step. The open-pr guard (ship-open-pr, decided by review-workflow-shape) exists so the built-in review workflow cannot be skipped before a PR; tying it to whether the workflow declares a review keeps that protection for every workflow that has one, and myteam-flow still has its own gate and owner sign-off before push. Deciding by declared step kinds rather than names honours the leaf's must_not on special-casing a workflow or step name.
fields.statement: Option (a): rhiza ship open-pr requires a journaled review only when the run's workflow declares one (a checks step, a workflow step running a review, or conduct checks). A workflow that declares no review, such as the BYO example myteam-flow, pushes after its own steps (gate, signoff) pass. A workflow that declares a review still refuses open-pr until it is journaled, so ship-change, bugfix and the other built-ins keep today's guard. The test is the workflow's declared shape, never its or a step's name. ship-open-pr's acceptance is reworded to match: a run whose workflow declares a review and has none journaled exits non-zero naming why; a run whose workflow declares none opens the PR.
